exercises.title: The Lighthouse Logbooks

exercises.text:

exercises.title: Why teenagers can't get up
exercises.text:
Most parents of teenagers will be (0) FAMILY familiar with the daily battle to get them out of bed on a school morning. During adolescence the body clock shifts, so that teenagers (57) NATURE .......... feel sleepy two or three hours later than adults do.

The problem is that school starts at the same time regardless. As a result, many teenagers get far less than the nine hours of sleep a night that (58) RESEARCH .......... recommend. Lack of sleep does more than cause (59) TIRED .......... in class. It can also affect memory and mood, and make young people more (60) PATIENT .......... with their friends and family.

Experts also warn that phones in the bedroom are (63) HELP .........., since the light from screens tells the brain that it is still daytime. Persuading teenagers to hand them over at night, of course, is another matter entirely.

exercises.title: Volunteering Abroad
exercises.text:

However, not every project is as useful as it appears. Some organisations charge (57) REASON .......... high fees, and a few send volunteers to do jobs for which they are completely (58) QUALIFY .......... and untrained. Before signing up, it is worth checking (59) CARE .......... what the money will be spent on and whether local people helped to plan the work. A good organisation will answer these questions without any (60) HESITATE .......... at all.

It is also important to be realistic. exercises.title: Two Wheels in the City
exercises.text:

However, not every scheme has been a success. In some cities the bikes turned out to be (59) RELY .........., with flat tyres, broken lights and chains that came off on hills. (60) FRUSTRATE .......... commuters soon gave up and went back to buses and cars, and a few schemes closed within a year.

exercises.title: Museums Without Walls
exercises.text:

Some museums offer (58) INTERACT .......... tours led by their own experts, while others use 3D scanning to copy objects so (59) ACCURATE .......... that viewers can zoom in on a single brushstroke or the scratches on an ancient coin. Children, who are often (60) ENTHUSIASM .......... fans of this kind of technology, can even 'pick up' and turn round objects that nobody is allowed to touch in real life.
